topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms, limitations, and resistance pathways associated with conventional interventions such as surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic tumor vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic strategies designed to exploit cancer-specific vulnerabilities including hormone dependence, checkpoint loss, and synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on inhibiting oncogenic kinase signaling pathways and managing the subsequent emergence of drug resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the use of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to selectively deliver cytotoxicity to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for immune surveillance and explore strategies to harness or genetically engineer T cells to eliminate cancer.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical clinical progress, persisting therapeutic challenges, and future paradigms in managing cancer.
